decisions.reason: Although it was no longer visibly marketed as a stand-alone item, it remains tightly linked to the firm's second-channel authentication core, so integration and refinement are more likely than withdrawal.
This security architecture is closest to the firm's established cryptography and platform capabilities, so high absorptive capacity favors continued development rather than exit.

The hardware signature token is related but less central to the firm's software-led identity strategy, and its lack of later visibility suggests limited traction and a likely redeployment of resources.
The compliance suite still fits the firm's regulated-security know-how, so despite weaker later visibility the firm is more likely to retain it and adapt it than remove it outright.
